title: The ZSDK developer API: classes, tunnels, lifecycle and notifications

prose.text: {{best-practices}} Error codes raised through `ZscalerError` and `ZscalerSDKException` are listed in [[shared.zsdk.error-codes]]. The repositories that carry the SDK are covered in [[shared.zsdk.sdk-integration]]. The help page and the code disagree on two class names {{divergence:class-names}}.

checks.do: Which tunnel the app started (Prelogin or Zero Trust) and the matching certificate lifetime, from the status call.
Whether the app handles the authentication-required notification by calling the Zero Trust start method with a fresh access token.
Whether the app calls suspend and resume at the platform-specific points.
Whether an Android WebView is given the proxy after the tunnel starts, and that its success listener fires before the first page load.

classes.statement: The ZSDK developer reference documents the classes ZscalerSDK (the primary class for ZSDK methods and properties), ZscalerConfiguration (the configurable properties), ZscalerProxyInfo (proxy details) and ZscalerError on iOS or ZscalerSDKException on Android (errors).

quotes: ZscalerSDK is the primary class for calling ZSDK key methods and properties.
ZscalerConfiguration is a configuration object with the following configurable ZSDK properties:
You can call on the following proxy configuration details from the ZscalerProxyInfo class:
ZscalerError for iOS and ZscalerSDKException for Android represent the following errors that can occur in ZSDK:

initialization.statement: On Android, `init` establishes the connection between the application and ZSDK and is required before calling other methods; iOS uses `sharedInstance()` to return the shared instance.

quotes: | init(application: Application, zscalerSDKConfiguration: ZscalerSDKConfiguration) | Android | Initializes to establish a connection between the application and ZSDK. This is required before calling other methods. |
| sharedInstance() | iOS | Returns the shared instance of ZSDK. |

tunnel-types.statement: `startPreLoginTunnel` takes the app key and device UDID and starts a Prelogin tunnel, for which Zscaler issues a client certificate valid for 180 days; `startZeroTrustTunnel` also takes an access token and starts a Zero Trust tunnel, whose client certificate is valid for 7 days. `stopTunnel()` terminates any active tunnels.

quotes: | startPreLoginTunnel(appKey: String, deviceUdid: String) | Starts a Prelogin tunnel. Zscaler issues a client certificate that is valid for 180 days. |
| startZeroTrustTunnel(appKey: String, deviceUdid: String, accessToken: String) | Starts a Zero Trust tunnel. Zscaler issues a client certificate that is valid for 7 days.
| stopTunnel() | Terminates any active tunnels from use. |

tunnel-upgrade.statement: From ZSDK version 2.0, `startZeroTrustTunnel()` can be called while a Prelogin tunnel is running, and ZSDK upgrades the existing tunnel connection to Zero Trust.

quotes: If you use ZSDK version 2.0 or later, the startZeroTrustTunnel() operation can be called even if a Prelogin tunnel is running. ZSDK upgrades the existing tunnel connection to Zero Trust.

tunnel-status.statement: `status()` returns a ZscalerSDKTunnelStatus with tunnelConnectionState (ON, OFF or CONNECTING) and tunnelType (0 Prelogin, 1 Zero Trust, -1 Unknown).

quotes: | status() | Returns the current ZSDK status as ZscalerSDKTunnelStatus object that comprises: tunnelConnectionState: The string status of the tunnel connection (ON, OFF, CONNECTING). tunnelType: The integer type of tunnel. 0: Prelogin 1: Zero Trust -1: Unknown |

configuration-properties.statement: ZscalerConfiguration properties include failIfDeviceCompromised, which prevents the mTLS tunnels on jailbroken or rooted devices, blockZPAConnectionsOnTunnelFailure, which blocks ZPA connections when any tunnel fails, useProxyAuthentication, and on iOS automatic configuration of URL sessions and WebViews.

quotes: | failIfDeviceCompromised | Boolean | All | If enabled, ZSDK prevents Mutual Transport Layer Security tunnels on jailbroken or rooted devices. |
| blockZPAConnectionsOnTunnelFailure | Boolean | All | If enabled, ZSDK blocks ZPA connections when any tunnels fail. |
| useProxyAuthentication | Boolean | All | If enabled, ZSDK allows proxy authentication. |
| shouldAutomaticallyConfigureRequests | Boolean | iOS | If enabled, ZSDK auto-configures URL sessions. |
| shouldAutomaticallyConfigureWebviews | Boolean | iOS | If enabled, ZSDK auto-configures WebViews. |

suspend-resume.statement: `suspend()` suspends ZSDK and stops active tunnels: on iOS it is called before app suspension, on Android when the app enters the background with no network operation pending or in progress. `resume()` is called when the app returns to the foreground (on Android, when it is ready to resume network operations).

quotes: Suspends ZSDK and stops active tunnels. For iOS, call this method before app suspension. For Android, call this method when the app enters the background and no network operation is pending or in progress.

Resumes ZSDK operations. For iOS, call this method when the app enters the foreground. For Android, call this method when the app is ready to resume network operations (i.e., when the app comes to the foreground).

maintenance.statement: `exportLogs` exports logs as a ZIP file, `clearLogs()` clears them, and `resetProxyPortAndRequireSessionRecreation()` resets the proxy port when setup fails, after which all HTTPS sessions and WebView requests must be recreated.

quotes: | exportLogs(destination: File Path) | Exports logs in a ZIP file to a specified location. |
| resetProxyPortAndRequireSessionRecreation() | Resets proxy port when setup fails. Requires recreation of all HTTPS (e.g., URL sessions) and WebView requests. |

notifications-state.statement: ZSDK reports tunnel state through notifications (Android enum, iOS NSNotification): `ZSCALERSDK_TUNNEL_CONNECTED` / `ZscalerSDKTunnelConnected` when the tunnel is ready and the app can send HTTPS and WebView traffic through it; `ZSCALERSDK_TUNNEL_DISCONNECTED` / `ZscalerSDKTunnelDisconnected` when it has stopped; `ZSCALERSDK_TUNNEL_RECONNECTING` / `ZscalerSDKTunnelReconnecting` when connecting to the Public Service Edge had an issue and ZSDK keeps trying.

quotes: ZscalerSDKNotificationEnum.ZSCALERSDK_TUNNEL_CONNECTED | NSNotification.ZscalerSDKTunnelConnected | The tunnel is in a connected state and ready for use for outbound network requests. Your application can send HTTPS and WebView traffic via the tunnel now.
ZscalerSDKNotificationEnum.ZSCALERSDK_TUNNEL_DISCONNECTED | NSNotification.ZscalerSDKTunnelDisconnected | Describes that the tunnel has stopped operations.

ZscalerSDKNotificationEnum.ZSCALERSDK_TUNNEL_RECONNECTING | NSNotification.ZscalerSDKTunnelReconnecting | There was an issue establishing a connection to the ZSDK Public Service Edge. ZSDK continues to connect and sends a Tunnel Connected notification if the connection is successfully established.

notifications-action.statement: Three notifications call for action: `ZSCALERSDK_TUNNEL_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` / `ZscalerSDKTunnelAuthenticationRequired` means the client certificate and proof of authentication or authorization have expired, resolved by calling `startZeroTrustTunnel()` with a new valid access token; `ZSCALERSDK_TUNNEL_RESOURCE_BLOCKED` / `ZscalerSDKTunnelResourceBlocked` means access is blocked by the access policy, resolved by making sure the application segment is configured; `ZSCALERSDK_PROXY_START_FAILED` / `ZscalerSDKProxyStartFailed` means proxy initialization failed, resolved by calling `resetProxyPortAndRequireSessionRecreation()`.

quotes: ZscalerSDKNotificationEnum.ZSCALERSDK_TUNNEL_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED | NSNotification.ZscalerSDKTunnelAuthenticationRequired | Either the client certificate and proof of authentication or authorization have expired.
Call the startZeroTrustTunnel() method to add a new, valid access token to re-authenticate the session.

ZscalerSDKNotificationEnum.ZSCALERSDK_TUNNEL_RESOURCE_BLOCKED | NSNotification.ZscalerSDKTunnelResourceBlocked | Access to the application is blocked as per the associated access policy. | Ensure the application segment is configured in the ZSDK Admin Portal.

ZscalerSDKNotificationEnum.ZSCALERSDK_PROXY_START_FAILED | NSNotification.ZscalerSDKProxyStartFailed | Proxy initialization has failed. | Call resetProxyPortAndRequireSessionRecreation() to retry the setup.

best-practices.statement: Zscaler recommends using the shared instance of the SDK class, setting ZscalerConfiguration before starting any tunnel, handling errors through ZscalerError or ZscalerSDKException and their codes, completing network operations before suspension, subscribing to tunnel-state notifications (BroadcastReceiver on Android, NSNotification on iOS), and exporting and clearing logs as needed.

quotes: Always use the shared instance of the ZscalerZSDK class for consistency across your applications.
Use ZscalerConfiguration prior to starting any tunnels.
Implement proper error handling using ZscalerError for iOS or ZscalerSDKException for Android, and their associated error codes.
Ensure network operations are complete before suspension.
Subscribe to ZscalerSDK notifications to monitor changes in the tunnel state by using platform-specific notification settings (e.g., BroadcastReceiver for Android, NSNotification for iOS).
Export and clear logs as needed for debugging and maintenance.

ios-header-types.statement: The iOS public headers declare ZscalerSDKProxyInfo (proxyHost, proxyPort and optional username and password, built with initWithHost:port:username:password:), ZscalerSDKTunnelStatus (a tunnelConnectionState string and a tunnelType) and the tunnel types ZscalerSDKTunnelTypeUnknown, ZscalerSDKTunnelTypePreLogin and ZscalerSDKTunnelTypeZeroTrust.

quotes: - (instancetype)initWithHost:(NSString*)host port:(NSInteger)port username:(nullable NSString*)username password:(nullable NSString*)password NS_DESIGNATED_INITIALIZER;

ios-notification-names.statement: The iOS headers declare the notification names ZscalerSDKTunnelDisconnected, ZscalerSDKTunnelConnected, ZscalerSDKTunnelReconnecting, ZscalerSDKTunnelAuthenticationRequired, ZscalerSDKTunnelResourceBlocked and ZscalerSDKProxyStartFailed, with the userInfo keys ZscalerSDKNotificationNameUserInfoKey and ZscalerSDKNotificationMessageUserInfoKey.

ios-proxy-start-failed.statement: The iOS header says ZscalerSDKProxyStartFailed means ZSDK failed to set up its proxy and requests using the proxy will fail; recovery is either to wait and try to restart the tunnel, or to call resetProxyPortAndRequireSessionRecreation() and then invalidate and recreate all ZSDK-configured sessions, which with automatic configuration means all URLSessions.

quotes: /// Indicates that ZscalerSDK has failed to set up it’s proxy. Requests using the proxy will fail.
///     Wait and try to restart the ZscalerSDK tunnel.
///     Call ZscalerSDK.resetProxyPortAndRequireSessionRecreation(), then invalidate and recreate all your ZscalerSDK-configured sessions.
/// If using automatic configuration, invalidate and recreate all URLSessions.

android-notification-broadcast.statement: In the Android sample app, notifications arrive as broadcasts: the app registers a receiver for the `ZscalerSDK.ZSCALER_RECEIVER_ID` action as not exported, reads the integer extra `ZscalerSDK.NOTIFICATION_CODE`, which it uses as an index into `ZscalerSDKNotificationEnum.values()`, and the string extra `ZscalerSDK.NOTIFICATION_MESSAGE`.

android-lifecycle-hooks.statement: The Android sample app registers a process lifecycle observer in Application.onCreate that calls `ZscalerSDK.resume()` on ON_START, as soon as the app comes to the foreground or network requests are going to be resumed, whichever is earlier, and `ZscalerSDK.suspend()` on ON_STOP, when the app goes to the background or ongoing network requests are finished, whichever is later.

quotes: // Call this as soon as app comes to foreground or network requests are going to be resumed, whichever is earlier.
// Call this when app goes to background or when ongoing network requests are finished, whichever is later.

android-init-errors.statement: The Android sample app calls `ZscalerSDK.init(application, ...)` in MainActivity.onCreate inside a try block that catches ZscalerSDKException and abandons startup on failure, can change settings afterwards with `ZscalerSDK.setConfiguration(...)`, and reads the numeric error from the exception's errorCode property.

quotes:
Log.e(TAG, "Got exception while initializing ZscalerSDK = $e")
            return

android-config-constructor.statement: The Android ZscalerSDKConfiguration is built with the named arguments useProxyAuthentication, failIfDeviceCompromised, blockZPAConnectionsOnTunnelFailure, enableDebugLogsInConsole and logLevel (a ZscalerSDKConfiguration.LogLevel); the sample app's defaults set failIfDeviceCompromised and enableDebugLogsInConsole to true and the log level to debug.

android-webview-manual-proxy.statement: In the Android sample app's manual mode, the app must call its WebView proxy setup after starting either tunnel so WebView traffic goes over the tunnel: it applies the host and port from ZscalerSDKProxyInfo through the androidx.webkit ProxyController (feature PROXY_OVERRIDE), and the code comment says WebView connections are not guaranteed to use the new proxy immediately, so wait for the success listener before loading a page.

quotes: * After starting either tunnel, this needs to be called for setting the web view proxy settings to route network traffic over the tunnel
* Note that as per android official docs, web view network connections are not guaranteed to
* immediately use the new proxy setting; wait for the success listener before loading a page.
* Set the web view proxy settings in manual mode
